definition: the deliberate investigation of social rules I ran at fourteen, and what it replaced

settled:
At fourteen I ran a deliberate conceptual investigation of the rules of social interaction, and it ran a year.

The wider way I built first contact started with observation of others, watching how social interaction worked before trying to run it. That year of study is one component of it.

It was a substitution rather than an extra. The route most people take social rules in by, picking them up while watching and never trying, is reduced in me. So I went at them explicitly and fitted what I found into what I already held.

That is the slower way in. A year of deliberate study against a childhood of incidental exposure.

It finishes higher. Rules arrived at explicitly are rules I can say out loud and can be shown wrong about, where rules absorbed without trying are neither.

title: The Year I Studied People On Purpose
